item.title: China to continue supporting Bangladesh’s defence modernization
item.description:
Chinese Ambassador to Bangladesh Yao Wen on Thursday reiterated China’s commitment to supporting the modernization of Bangladesh’s defence sector.
He made the remarks during a courtesy call on Defence Adviser Brigadier General (retd) Dr AKM Shamsul Islam at his office at the Armed Forces Division in Dhaka Cantonment, according to the Inter-Services Public Relation Directorate (ISPR).
During the meeting, the two sides discussed ways to further strengthen existing military and defence cooperation between Bangladesh and China.
They particularly discussed advanced professional training for members of the two countries’ armed forces, exchanges in military education and enhancing technical capabilities.
They expressed hope that greater exchanges of experience and expanded training cooperation to address modern military challenges would further strengthen defence ties between the two countries.
The defence adviser highlighted the long-standing friendly relations and strategic partnership between Bangladesh and China, as well as China’s support for Bangladesh’s development. He expressed hope that bilateral cooperation would expand further in the future.
The Chinese ambassador reaffirmed China’s commitment to continued cooperation and support for the modernization of Bangladesh’s defence sector.
The two sides also expressed their resolve to expand defence cooperation in areas of mutual interest and further strengthen Bangladesh-China relations.

item.title: Iranian students in limbo as sanctions halt GRE, Toefl tests
item.description:
Iranian students hoping to study abroad are facing a new obstacle after Toefl and GRE testing was suspended inside the country following changes to US sanctions regulations.
“My entire plan was built around taking this exam,” a Toefl candidate in Tehran told DW.
She said she had spent months preparing applications for a PhD program, contacting professors and gathering documents despite internet disruptions and other challenges.
ETS, the US-based organization that administers both exams, announced it suspended testing in Iran after the US Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (Ofac) froze General License G, which had allowed certain educational services to continue in Iran.
“Following Ofac’s suspension of General License G, ETS has paused administration of the Toefl and GRE tests in Iran effective immediately,” the organization said in an official notice.
ETS added that Iranian nationals can still take the exams outside Iran and that it is exploring options to restore testing.
Toefl is a US-based English-language proficiency test accepted by universities worldwide. The GRE is a standardized test required by some graduate programs, particularly in the United States and Canada.
Since the Iran war began in late February, the US has increasingly expanded sanctions targeting Iranian trade and exports, contributing to broader disruptions throughout the Iranian economy.
An Iranian institution that administered Toefl exams told DW that new registrations had stopped following the latest sanctions changes.
The institution added that the suspension could be temporary, but no date had been given for exams to resume.
That uncertainty is particularly serious for students approaching university and scholarship deadlines who have spent months preparing and paying application-related costs.
The suspension follows earlier problems with Ielts (British equivalent of Toefl) testing in Iran. An Ielts center in Tehran told DW that sanctions-related difficulties transferring money had become one of the main obstacles to continuing exams.
Some Iranian applicants had already been traveling to countries such as Turkiye and Armenia to take Ielts. Toefl and GRE candidates may now have to do the same.
Alireza, who is preparing to apply to a university in Italy, said the suspension of Toefl had disrupted a backup plan he had arranged after Ielts testing became unavailable.
“European universities usually accept Ielts. But because Ielts has been suspended in Iran, after extensive correspondence with the university, they agreed to let [Iranian students] meet the required score through an equivalent Toefl result,” he told DW.
“But now Toefl has also been suspended in Iran. Traveling to a neighboring country just to take the exam is very expensive, especially given Iran’s current economic situation,” added Alireza.
Another candidate told DW that taking the exam in Turkiye or Armenia would mean paying for travel and at least one night’s accommodation on top of the test fee.
For students hoping to secure scholarships or full funding, those additional expenses can be significant.
Iranian Toefl and GRE candidates have launched an online petition urging ETS to restore access to the exams.
The petition says thousands of students are losing access to tests required for university admissions, scholarships, graduate programs and other academic opportunities. Many, it says, have spent months preparing, paid exam-related costs and built their application schedules around specific test dates.
“Students should not lose years of preparation or their chance to pursue higher education because access to required examinations has suddenly been removed,” the petition states.
Narges, an Iranian applicant affected by the suspension, said she had seen the petition circulating in Telegram groups used by language learners and students applying to foreign universities.
“I doubt it will have any impact,” she said. “Still, I’m going to sign the petition.”
The organizers are calling on Ofac to provide a specific exemption for standardized academic testing, and on ETS to restore Toefl and GRE services in Iran as soon as legally possible.
They argue that sanctions aimed at the Iranian government should not restrict educational opportunities for ordinary citizens who have no role in state policy.
Until recently, the General License G had provided a legal channel for certain academic exchanges and educational services despite broader US sanctions on Iran.
For many students, the suspension is the latest in a series of barriers to studying abroad.
Bahar, who is applying for PhD programs, said many Iranian students had already shifted their focus from the United States because obtaining visas had become increasingly difficult.
“American universities were our first choice because they generally offer funding for PhD programs more readily than European universities,” she told DW.
Now, she said, applicants are increasingly turning to Europe and Australia, but the testing suspension has created a new hurdle.
“There is effectively no difference between Ielts and Toefl for us now, because in either case, we have to leave Iran to take an English language test,” Bahar said.
For students approaching admissions deadlines, postponement may not simply mean waiting a few months. It can mean missing an entire admissions cycle, losing scholarship opportunities or delaying academic plans by a year or more.
While ETS says it is examining possible ways to restore testing in Iran, there is currently no indication of when that might happen. For many applicants, the immediate choice is limited: wait without knowing when testing will return, or spend considerably more to take the same exam abroad.

item.title: Minister Millat’s vehicle fined after driving on wrong side in Dhaka
item.description:
Traffic police stopped a vehicle carrying Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat in Dhaka on Thursday morning after it was allegedly found driving on the wrong side of the road, filing two cases and imposing Tk 6,000 in fines.
The incident took place after 9am when the Range Rover, bearing registration number Dhaka Metro-Gha-18-2125, was traveling toward the Secretariat after passing in front of Kakrail Mosque, according to sources familiar with the incident.
A Traffic Ramna Division official wishing to be anonymous, said the vehicle had violated its lane and was obstructing normal traffic movement. The official said traffic police stopped the vehicle in front of the Secretariat and informed its driver, Arif Hossain, that driving on the wrong side of the road in such a manner was a violation of traffic rules.
The official said the vehicle was carrying a flag and that the minister was inside when traffic police stopped it. A traffic officer on duty subsequently detained the vehicle, and the cases were filed in the presence of senior officials.
Traffic Sergeant Sifat Mahmud, who was on duty at the time, filed the two cases.
The two cases carry fines of Tk 3,000 each, totaling Tk 6,000. One case was filed for creating an obstruction to traffic movement, while the other was for driving the vehicle unsafely.
Speaking to the media about the incident, Sergeant Sifat said: “I could not believe that a case could be filed against a minister’s vehicle. It is a rare incident.”
He said the traffic control room had also been informed about the incident and that the Special Security Force (SSF) had instructed them to take action.
“The driver of the vehicle also admitted to violating traffic rules,” Sifat said.

item.title: PM greets Hindu community on Janmashtami
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday greeted the members of the Hindu community in Bangladesh and around the world on the occasion of Janmashtami to be celebrated on Friday.
In a message, he urged people of all faiths to play a conscious and responsible role in maintaining social order, brotherhood and communal harmony and remain vigilant against any attempt to disrupt the peaceful atmosphere.
“I urge everyone to be vigilant so that no one can destroy this atmosphere of harmony,” he said.
The prime minister described Janmashtami as a significant religious occasion for Hindus and extended greetings to Hindu brothers and sisters and followers of Sanatan Dharma.
Referring to Hindu scriptures, he said Lord Krishna was born in Mathura on the eighth day of the waning fortnight of the lunar month during the reign of the tyrant King Kansa.
Krishna later ended Kansa’s oppressive rule, upheld righteousness and fought evil, he said.
The prime minister said Krishna’s life and teachings embody humanism, justice, equality and peace, while his ideals of devotion, human welfare and harmony continue to inspire people.
He said people of different religions and beliefs in Bangladesh have been practicing their faiths with mutual respect and harmony from ancient age.
He expressed hope that the ideals of Shri Krishna would further strengthen mutual harmony and brotherhood in the society.
The prime minister wished happiness, peace and prosperity for all on the occasion of Janmashtami.

item.title: Police: Five arrested with weapons over planned Banani robbery
item.description:
Five people have been arrested in Banani while allegedly preparing to commit a robbery, police said.
The arrestees were identified as Md Masud Rana, 29; Md Rajib Hawladar, 30; Hafizul Matbar, 24; Mohammad Shakil Hossain, 24; and Md Badal, 42.
Additional Police Commissioner (DB) Md Shafiqul Islam disclosed the information at a press conference at the DMP Media Centre on Thursday afternoon.
A foreign-made pistol, a magazine, a walkie-talkie, a pair of handcuffs bearing the Bangladesh Police emblem and other items allegedly intended for use in the robbery were recovered from them. Police also seized a Hiace microbus.
Gulshan Division of the Detective Branch received information around 9:30am that a group was preparing to carry out a robbery on Road No 4 in the Banani police station area, said the DMP official.
Acting on the tip-off, a 45-member DB team took position in the area and later conducted a raid in front of Khayer Palace on Road No 4, where the five suspects were arrested.
During the operation, police recovered a foreign-made pistol, a magazine, a walkie-talkie, a pair of handcuffs bearing the Bangladesh Police emblem, a roll of black adhesive tape, a shopping bag and the Hiace microbus.
The DB is interrogating the suspects to determine why they had gathered in the area and to establish details of their alleged robbery plan.
Investigators are also looking into whether the suspects are members of an organized criminal group, the source of the firearm, and whether they have previous criminal records or links to other offenses, police said.
Legal proceedings against the suspects are being initiated at Banani Police Station. Police are also continuing operations to identify and arrest others allegedly involved with the group.

item.title: Dengue: Four more die as 1,252 cases recorded in 24 hours
item.description:
Health officials on Thursday said they recorded 1,252 fresh cases of dengue onslaughts killing at least four persons in the past 24 hours.
"During the period, (of the 1,252) 119 patients were hospitalized in Barisal division, 194 in Chittagong division, 227 in Dhaka division, 135 in Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) and 101 in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) areas, 247 in Khulna division, 87 in Mymensingh division, 109 in Rajshahi division, 27 in Rangpur division and six in Sylhet division, a Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) statement said.
Since the start of the dengue onslaughts Bangladesh this year witnessed so far 111 deaths while the disease inflicted 39,532.
The dengue last year claimed 413 lives and inflicted 1,02,861 people in the country.
Besides, the dengue claimed 575 lives and inflicted 1,01,214 people in 2024.

item.title: AIUB founding chairman Anwarul Abedin’s 14th death anniversary Sept 5
item.description:
The 14th death anniversary of Dr Anwarul Abedin, founder chairman of American International University-Bangladesh (AIUB), will be observed on Saturday, September 5, 2026.
To mark the occasion, Dr Abedin’s family and the AIUB community will organize a Qur’an recitation, prayer and Milad Mahfil on the university campus.
The AIUB community has sought prayers from students, faculty members, officers, staff, relatives and well-wishers for the eternal peace and salvation of his departed soul.
Dr Anwarul Abedin was an educationist who played a pioneering role in the development of higher education in Bangladesh.
He founded AIUB with a vision of expanding access to quality higher education and establishing an institution of international standards.
On his death anniversary, the AIUB community will pay respect to his memory and remember his contributions to the development of higher education in Bangladesh.

item.title: Russia to close branches of Germany’s Goethe Institute
item.description:
Russia will close multiple branches of Germany’s Goethe Institute in response to Germany ordering the closure of a Russian cultural center in Berlin, Moscow said Thursday, amid spiraling tensions between the two countries.
The Goethe Institute, funded by Germany’s foreign office, is a nonprofit organization that promotes the study of the German language.
The announcement comes after Germany imposed sanctions on Moscow this week -- including the closure of a cultural center in Berlin -- accusing it of an attempted “hybrid attack” on Leipzig airport last month.
Russia has described Germany’s allegations as unsubstantiated and “absurd.”
“The Germans have branches of the Goethe Institute here... Of course, they’ll be closed once our cultural center has been forced out over there,” Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said, according to the state Tass news agency.
He said the group’s branches in Moscow, Saint Petersburg and Yekaterinburg would be closed, although the Goethe Institute does not list a branch in Yekaterinburg on its website.
Germany said it regretted Russia’s decision.
“The Goethe Institute... has played an important role in Russia as a cultural bridge, and we would have been prepared to continue that,” German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul told reporters.
Tensions between the two countries have soared since Berlin accused Moscow of being behind a drone incident at Leipzig airport last month.
Russia summoned Germany’s charge d’affaires on Wednesday over what it called Berlin’s “anti-Russian actions” in response to the incident.

item.title: Trump ‘happy’ Prince Harry and Meghan have left US
item.description:
President Donald Trump said Wednesday he was glad Prince Harry and his wife Meghan Markle had left the United States -- while adding that if he were part of the British royal family, he would not have taken them back.
Trump accused Meghan, 45, of being “terribly disrespectful” to the late Queen Elizabeth II, in his first reaction since the prince and his American wife moved back to Britain from California.
The A-list celebrity couple is now settling in back in Harry’s homeland, six years after they stepped down as working royals and left for the United States amid bitter acrimony with his family.
“I’m happy about it. I was not a fan,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office when asked what he thought about Harry and Meghan’s departure.
“I thought they treated the royal family with great disrespect. I didn’t like it. I didn’t like the way she acted. I thought she was terribly disrespectful to the Queen, to King Charles.”
Harry, 41, appeared to have mended relations with his father, King Charles III, who is battling cancer, during more recent UK visits.
Harry reportedly remains estranged from Prince William, his brother and heir to the throne, and William’s wife Catherine.
Trump said he wouldn’t have been so forgiving.
“Maybe I’m different. I wouldn’t have taken him back, right? If I were the royal family, I would not have taken them back,” said Trump.
The 80-year-old former reality TV star has previously traded barbs with Meghan on a number of occasions.
On the eve of a state visit to Britain in 2019 during his first term, Trump denied that he had called Meghan “nasty,” despite the comment being clearly audible on a tape of an interview with a tabloid.
She had in turn been critical of Trump during the 2016 presidential campaign, calling him “misogynistic” and “divisive.”
Trump again seemed stung when Meghan commented ahead of the 2020 election, which he lost, saying he was “not a fan” and adding: “I wish a lot of luck to Harry, because he’s going to need it.”
The royal couple’s return to Britain along with their children Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, marked the end of a long exile from Harry’s homeland.
The pair married in a glitzy wedding in 2018 but two years later relinquished their role as working royals after a feud with the British royals and moved to North America.
The rift then deepened as Harry published his tell-all memoir “Spare” and the couple gave a no-holds-barred interview to US talk show hostess Oprah Winfrey.
Meghan, who is mixed-race, and Harry insinuated to Winfrey that the monarchy was racist, claiming a family member raised a question about the skin color of their son before he was born.
Meghan also said she had contemplated suicide after joining the royal family.
But while the couple signed a string of commercial deals with US platforms like Netflix and Spotify, reports said their attempts to make a living in the United States had fallen flat.
Their return to Britain has raised a number of questions.
The Telegraph newspaper reported that the couple plan to stay for “an extended period,” living in a home in the Cotswolds region, in central England, having enrolled their children at a school for the coming academic year.
But with speculation rampant around their reasons for returning and whether the stay is permanent, reports have noted the couple intend to keep their existing homes in California and Portugal.
Meghan faces a particularly tough challenge in reassimilating to life in Britain, where she remains unpopular. Polling shows a majority of people hold unfavorable views of her and, to a lesser extent, Harry.

item.title: SOS Children’s Villages Bangladesh, Commercial Bank of Ceylon to train youths in digital marketing
item.description:
SOS Children’s Villages Bangladesh and Commercial Bank of Ceylon PLC Bangladesh Operations have partnered to provide professional digital marketing training to young people from economically disadvantaged backgrounds.
A cheque handover ceremony marking the partnership was held at the Head Office of Commercial Bank of Ceylon in Dhaka.
Commercial Bank of Ceylon PLC Bangladesh Operations was represented by the chief executive officer Tivanka Damunupola; deputy CEO and head of corporate banking Mahmud Hossain; deputy CEO and COO Haily Algewatte; and head of sustainability and women banking Urmi Irani Khan.
SOS Children’s Villages Bangladesh was represented by national director Dr Md Enamul Haque; deputy director of fund development and communications Rashal Mia; and corporate fundraising officer Arman Kabir Mahid.
The program is designed to equip young people who have limited access to education and employment opportunities with practical, job-relevant digital marketing skills.
Participants will learn from experienced trainers through hands-on sessions reflecting current workplace practices and industry needs.
In addition to technical training, participants will receive career guidance and job-placement support upon completing the course.
Dr Md Enamul Haque, national director of SOS Children’s Villages Bangladesh, said: “Practical skills can open new possibilities for a young person’s future. With the support of Commercial Bank of Ceylon PLC, participants will leave the course not only with digital marketing knowledge but also with clearer pathways to employment or entrepreneurship. We are grateful for this partnership and its investment in young people’s independence.”
Tivanka Damunupola, chief executive officer of Commercial Bank of Ceylon PLC Bangladesh operations, said: “Access to relevant skills can significantly expand a young person’s opportunities. Digital marketing offers diverse career pathways in Bangladesh and beyond, including employment, freelancing and entrepreneurship. By supporting this course, we are investing directly in the potential of young people and look forward to seeing them build sustainable careers and businesses.”
Through the partnership, SOS Children’s Villages Bangladesh and CBC aim to enable young people with limited opportunities to acquire relevant skills and participate meaningfully in Bangladesh’s growing digital economy.
The training is scheduled to begin in mid-September 2026 at the SOS Vocational Training Centre, Dhaka.

item.title: Islami Bank, Jagannath University Ink MoU for co-branded master debit cards

Md Maznuzzaman and Md Mosharraf Hossain, executive vice presidents, Muzahidul Islam, senior vice president, along with senior officials from both organizations attended the ceremony.

item.title: Green Dot & KSB to bring water management solutions to Bangladesh
item.description:
Bangladesh’s rapidly growing urban population and expanding industrial sector are creating greater demand for efficient water supply, wastewater treatment and water reuse.
This is increasing the importance of energy-efficient technologies and sustainable water infrastructure.
German pump and valve manufacturer KSB Ltd and Green Dot Limited, a concern of ZI Group, jointly organized the “Solutions for Sustainable Water Management” program on September 2 at Radisson Hotel Dhaka.
Discussions focused on modern pumping and flow-management technologies for water collection and transportation, water supply, wastewater treatment and water reuse.
Participants also discussed ways to reduce energy consumption, improve operational efficiency and optimize lifecycle costs.
Vice president of KSB Germany Philip Storch highlighted the role of advanced pumping technology in improving the efficiency and reliability of water infrastructure.
He said KSB aims to provide solutions that help customers improve operational performance, reduce energy and maintenance costs, and achieve sustainable long-term results.
Sr general manager & regional sales manager from KSB Jyotirmoy S Bose spoke about the importance of advanced pumping technology in building more efficient and reliable water infrastructure.
He said that KSB’s solutions can help improve system performance, reduce energy consumption and maintenance costs, and support the long-term sustainability of water and wastewater management.
ABM Zahidul Islam, chairman of Green Dot Ltd, emphasized the importance of combining global technology with local engineering expertise to address Bangladesh’s growing water management needs.
He said the collaboration with KSB will create opportunities to bring advanced pumping and flow-management solutions to the country and support the development of more efficient and sustainable water infrastructure.
The program also created an opportunity for local professionals and international technology specialists to exchange knowledge and experience, particularly on adapting modern technologies to Bangladesh’s water and infrastructure requirements.
Several distinguished officials and professionals from the water and infrastructure sectors also spoke on the occasion, including Md Khalekujjaman, chief engineer of the Public Works Department (PWD); Ahteshamul Rasel Khan, additional chief engineer of the Department of Public Health Engineering (DPHE); Md Abdul Kaium, SE, Planning Circle; Saifur Rahman, project director, GOB/Unicef, DPHE; Dr Muhit of the Gates Foundation; Dr Mohammad Saif Uddin, additional chief engineer, DPHE; and Mohammad Vadrul Alam, chief engineer of the Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC), alongside other distinguished engineers and sector professionals.
The event was attended by Nargis Sultana, managing director of Green Dot Limited, along with senior officials from KSB India, including Jyotirmoy S Bose, senior general manager & regional sales manager (East Zone); Meena Kumari, export manager; Philip Storch, vice president, sales management water; and Sunil Bapat, vice president–operations, Sinnar Plant & Foundry Division and COO, Solar Pumps.
SM Saidul Alam, country manager–Bangladesh, KSB, was also present at the event.
The KSB–Green Dot initiative brings together international technological expertise and local engineering and market knowledge, creating opportunities for more efficient and sustainable water infrastructure development in Bangladesh.

item.title: Rajkumar Hirani confirms 3 Idiots sequel is in development
item.description:
Rajkumar Hirani has confirmed that a sequel to “3 Idiots” is in development, with Aamir Khan, R Madhavan and Sharman Joshi set to reprise their roles.
Speaking to ANI, Hirani said the team is currently working on the script and will only proceed once they are satisfied with the story.
“Kahani likhi jaa rahi hai; we are still writing. Once it reaches the right point, then we will talk about it. Abhi toh we are still writing. Casting will be the same,” Hirani said.
The filmmaker revealed that the sequel emerged from a story he and his team were developing separately. During the writing process, they realized the idea could fit into the world of “3 Idiots”.
“We were writing another story, and then it felt like the story we had written would fit into this second part,” Hirani explained.
Unlike the 2009 film, which followed three engineering students during their college years, the proposed sequel will move the story forward by around 20 years.
“It’s not about the students; it’s about 20 years later ab kya hota hai unki life main,” Hirani said.
The original film starred Aamir Khan as Rancho, R Madhavan as Farhan, and Sharman Joshi as Raju. Kareena Kapoor Khan, Boman Irani, and Omi Vaidya were also part of the cast.
Hirani, however, stressed that the sequel has not been finalized yet. The project will move forward only if the writing reaches a stage where he and his team are confident in the story.
“3 Idiots”, released in 2009, became one of the highest-grossing Hindi films of its time and remains one of Hirani’s most widely celebrated films.

item.title: Charli XCX brings new era to Reading Festival stage
item.description:
Charli XCX brought her latest musical era to Reading Festival on Friday with a set that combined songs from “Music, Fashion, Film,” “Brat,” and her earlier work.
The performance marked her first UK festival appearance since releasing “Music, Fashion, Film,” which moves toward a stronger rock influence following the electronic pop sound of “Brat.”
Charli opened with “Rock Music” before performing new tracks, including “Wink Wink,” “Yeah,” and “Card Declined.”
She then moved through different stages of her career, performing “Track 10” from her 2017 mixtape and “House,” which she co-wrote for the “Wuthering Heights” soundtrack.
The set also included “Club Classics,” “365,” and “Von Dutch” from “Brat,” the 2024 album that became a cultural phenomenon and earned Charli a Grammy.
The production was more elaborate than her previous “Brat” tour, featuring multiple costume changes, pyrotechnics, strobe lighting, dancers, and a live band. Distorted black-and-white visuals appeared throughout the performance.
Charli closed the set with “No One Lasts Forever,” the final track from “Music, Fashion, Film.” The song ends with a spoken contribution from filmmaker David Cronenberg reflecting on mortality and oblivion.
Irish rock band Fontaines DC performed after Charli on the main stage. Despite a delay of around 30 minutes, the group drew a strong response with songs including “Favourite,” “I Love You,” and “Starbuster.”
Earlier, grime artist Skepta performed through heavy rain, energizing the crowd with “Praise the Lord (Da Shine)” and “Victory Lap.”
Other performers included US rock band Geese, singer Skye Newman, and Jamie T.
Reading and Leeds festivals feature 6 major headliners this year, with Dave, Raye, Chase & Status, and Florence + The Machine among the acts scheduled to headline across the weekend.

item.title: Ariana Grande wraps up tour ahead of public break
item.description:
Ariana Grande ended her 41-date “Eternal Sunshine” tour with an emotional final performance at London’s O2 Arena on Tuesday, September 1, before beginning an extended break from public appearances.
The singer became visibly emotional during several performances, including “One Last Time," which has particular significance for survivors and families affected by the 2017 Manchester terror attack.
Addressing the London audience, Grande thanked fans for their support and described the tour as one of the most extraordinary experiences of her life.
“I’ll cherish this experience always,” she told the crowd, adding that she was grateful to have the “best fans in the entire world."
Grande had announced last month that she would step back from public-facing activities after the tour. Her representatives said the decision followed continued public scrutiny and was intended to allow her to take a break.
The singer has also withdrawn from the upcoming West End production of Stephen Sondheim’s “Sunday in the Park with George”, in which she had been scheduled to appear alongside her “Wicked” co-star Jonathan Bailey. Bailey subsequently announced his own departure from the production.
Despite the emotional moments, Grande delivered a largely energetic performance throughout her final show. A foot injury meant she had to replace her trademark stilettos with knee-high platform boots, but she continued performing alongside her dancers.
The Eternal Sunshine tour marked Grande’s return to the stage after a seven-year absence. Her 10-show London residency attracted fans from around the world and brought the tour to a close after performances across North America and the UK.
Grande had previously described the tour as a “last hurrah” and said she wanted to devote more time to acting following her Oscar-nominated performance in “Wicked”.
The London shows received largely positive reviews, with critics praising Grande’s vocals, stage presence, and production. However, some also expressed concern over the intense public scrutiny surrounding her appearance.
Grande has rejected the suggestion that her decision to step back was prompted by the criticism. She previously described the move as a planned and deliberate decision, saying, "Boundaries need to be set; human beings do need a break sometimes.”
During the final show, Grande ended the performance with a theatrical exit, ascending above the stage as fans watched on.
It remains unclear when she will return to touring or regular public appearances. For now, the singer is set to take a break following the conclusion of her “Eternal Sunshine” tour.

item.title: When Luca returned, so did our humanity
item.description:
As a theater enthusiast, one of the questions I am often asked is how I measure the success of a play. Is it the applause? The standing ovation? The ticket sales?
On the evening of August 29, at Toronto's Fairview Library Theatre, I found my answer.
After Return of Luca ended, audience members remained seated. Some wiped tears from their eyes. Others struggled to express what they were feeling. A few openly wept as they shared their thoughts. In that moment, I realized that Luca's story had travelled beyond the stage and found a place in people's hearts.
For me, Return of Luca was never simply a play about a teenager with special needs. It was a story about families—families who love deeply, sacrifice quietly, and carry hopes and fears that often remain unseen by the wider world.
Emam, Emu, and Raisa share a poignant family moment in Return of Luca, portraying the love, resilience, and challenges at the heart of the story. Photo:Courtesy
We often notice the challenges faced by a child with special needs, but we do not always see the parents who spend sleepless nights worrying about the future. We do not see the siblings who grow up learning patience and compassion beyond their years. Nor do we see the countless acts of resilience that take place behind closed doors every day.
I wanted to bring those stories into the light.
The inspiration for Return of Luca came not only from observation but also from personal experience. Like many families, my own has lived through the realities of supporting a child with special needs. I have witnessed the love, exhaustion, uncertainty, and determination that shape such journeys. Writing this play gave voice to experiences that are too often overlooked.
Toronto Theatre Folks presented the play in partnership with Progressive Action for Community Empowerment (PACE) and the University of Toronto, creating a platform for a broader conversation about inclusion, understanding, and community responsibility.
What moved me most on opening night was seeing how audiences connected with the story. People did not respond because Luca's life was extraordinary; they responded because it felt familiar. They recognized a son, a daughter, a neighbor, a friend, or perhaps even themselves in the characters on stage.
Under the sensitive direction of Naila Azad Nupur, the production avoided sentimentality and focused instead on honesty. Nuha's remarkable performance in the title role, supported by a dedicated ensemble cast, brought authenticity and humanity to every scene.
Emam, Emu, and Raisa navigate a difficult and emotional moment, reflecting the struggles faced by families caring for a loved one with special needs. Photo:Collected
Emu, as Luca's mother; Emam, as his father; and Raisa, as his sister, convincingly portrayed a family bound by love and challenged by uncertainty. Moumita, as Luca's friend, and Sabita, as Sara, added warmth and compassion, while Afsana and Azmain effectively reflected the importance of community support. The chorus ensemble—Bonani, Abantika, and Brinda—beautifully conveyed the emotional undercurrents of the story and enriched its visual and poetic dimensions. Together, they transformed words on a page into living emotions. Naila Azad Nupur's music and choreography further deepened the play's emotional resonance.
At its heart, Return of Luca asks a simple but important question: Do we see people for their limitations or for their humanity? Too often, society defines individuals with special needs by what they cannot do. Yet behind every silence is a world of dreams, emotions, fears, and possibilities. Every person has a story worth hearing.
Perhaps that is why the word "return" in the title carries a meaning beyond Luca himself. It represents a return to empathy, understanding, and compassion. It invites us to see one another more fully and to build communities where no one is left behind.
As audience members left the theater that evening, many carried Luca's story with them. For a playwright, there is no greater reward.
The performance may have ended, but the conversation had only begun. If Luca remains in the hearts of those who watched him, then perhaps he has accomplished what every story hopes to achieve: reminding us of our shared humanity.
Emamul Haque is a cultural activist, playwright, and former United Nations staff member based in Toronto.

item.title: On his centenary, five films of Uttam Kumar to watch
item.description:
A hundred years since his birth, the question of where to start with Uttam Kumar’s filmography can feel almost unfair—the man made more than 200 films across three decades. But five of them, watched in order, trace something more useful than a highlight reel: the arc of how a failed clerk-turned-actor became “Mahanayak,” and how he kept reinventing what that title meant even after the industry thought it had him figured out.
Before this film, Uttam Kumar was, in the industry’s own words, a “flop master”—two failed releases behind him, his career hanging by a thread. “Sharey Chuattar” didn’t just reverse that. It paired him for the first time with Suchitra Sen, and the chemistry between them was immediate enough that it became the template for Bengali romantic cinema for the next twenty years. Watching it now, it’s less about the plot than about catching the exact moment a partnership was born—before either of them knew what they were building.
By the time this amnesia drama arrived, the Uttam-Suchitra pairing had already become something close to its own genre—soft-focus close-ups, sweeping heartbreak, love thwarted by circumstance before finding its way back. “Harano Sur” is the pairing at full confidence, unhurried, and fully aware of its own appeal. It’s a useful reminder that melodrama, done with this much control, doesn’t age the way melodrama usually does.
Here, Uttam Kumar stepped behind the camera as producer as well as star, and the result is arguably the most enduring film of his career—a college love story that Bengali audiences still quote from memory. What makes “Saptapadi” worth revisiting isn’t just the romance; it’s the evidence of an actor who had started shaping his own image deliberately, rather than simply accepting whatever the studios handed him.
Satyajit Ray’s “Nayak” is where the matinee idol turned the camera on himself. Uttam Kumar plays a film star confronting the hollowness underneath his own celebrity—a role that only worked because audiences already knew him as exactly that kind of star. It’s a rare case of an actor’s real-life persona becoming the raw material for a film, and Ray trusted him enough to hand him the risk.
Also directed by Ray, and about as far from romantic-hero territory as Uttam Kumar ever travelled—a private detective story that, alongside “Antony Firingee” the same year, won him the first-ever National Film Award for Best Actor. No actor since has repeated the feat of winning it for two films in a single year. “Chiriyakhana” is the clearest proof that the man Bengal knew as its biggest commercial star could hold his own in a genre exercise from its most demanding auteur—and make it look like no effort at all.

item.title: Madrasa teacher arrested over rape allegation in Narayanganj
item.description:
Police have arrested a madrasa teacher in Fatullah, Narayanganj, over an allegation of raping a 17-year-old student.
The accused, Md Rafiqul Islam, 28, was arrested from Tahsinul Quran Madrasa in Muslim Nagar on Wednesday after local residents detained him and called the national emergency service 999.
Fatullah Model Police Station Inspector (Investigation) Anwar Hossain confirmed the arrest to Dhaka Tribune on Thursday afternoon.
He said the student’s father filed a case at the police station over the allegation. The student was sent to a hospital for a medical examination, while police have started investigating the case.
According to police, a resident of Muslim Nagar called 999 on Wednesday afternoon and reported that a teacher at the madrasa had allegedly raped a 17-year-old student.
The report prompted local residents to detain and beat the teacher, creating tension in the area. The emergency service subsequently informed Fatullah police station and requested police intervention.
A police team later went to the madrasa and arrested Rafiqul with the help of local residents before taking him to the police station.
Police sources said the student had completed Hifz, or memorization of the Quran, and enrolled at Tahsinul Quran Madrasa about a year ago to further improve his Quran memorization.
According to the allegations, Rafiqul had been sexually abusing the student for about a year by intimidating him.
The latest alleged assault took place on the night of August 31, after which the student fell ill, police sources said.
The student’s mother took him home for treatment. After learning about the alleged assault, she and local residents went to the madrasa and confronted the teacher.
Rafiqul is the son of the late Abdul Mannan of Barunda village under Tongibari police station in Munshiganj. He had been working as a teacher at Tahsinul Quran Madrasa in Muslim Nagar, Fatullah.
The information was provided in a statement issued by the national emergency service 999.

item.title: President urges expatriates to contribute to country’s development
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Thursday called upon Bangladeshi business people living abroad to further contribute to the country’s development by investing their money and making efforts to bring more foreign investment in the country.
The president made the call when a delegation of Bangladeshi expatriates living in the United Kingdom paid a courtesy call on him at Bangabhaban on Thursday afternoon, President’s Press Wing sources said.
Led by UK-based prominent businessman Kamal Uddin, the delegation congratulated Mirza Fakrul on assuming the office of the president.
The president gratefully recalled immense contribution of the expatriates to the movement for establishing democracy and justice in the country through investing their money, labour and intellect, saying “the country and its people would always remember your contribution and role.”
The president also expressed gratitude to the expatriates, noting that their remittances are one of the major driving forces of the country’s economy.
During the meeting, the delegation sought the president’s support to enhance business opportunities and civic facilities for them, including addressing the issue of harassment in the airports. They also urged for ensuring their voting rights in the country.
President Fakhrul Islam said, the government has already started working to resolve these problems and enhance civic facilities for the expatriates.
"Probashi Card has been introduced to ensure comprehensive service facilities and benefits for the expatriates,” he said.
He also urged expat Bangladeshis to invest more in the country, contribute to employment generation, education, healthcare, technology and skill development and other social welfare activities.
The delegation expressed interest in investing in the country.
President’s military secretary and press secretary were present at the meeting.
